title: Start fresh or pick up later

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
You'll learn how to pick up a conversation even after closing Claude Code, and how to start fresh.

First — what is a "conversation"?

Everything you and Claude say after you start Claude Code is a conversation. Within the same conversation, Claude remembers what was said, so "that file from earlier" is enough.

If a conversation gets very long, Claude can get confused, so it's best to start a new conversation when you start a different task.

  • Time: 10 minutes
  • You need: the computer you used for Terminal practice 1

faq.q: Does clearing the conversation delete my files?
faq.a: No. Only your messages with Claude go away. Files like todo.txt stay as they are.

steps.title: Which computer are you using?
steps.html: Pick the computer you used for Terminal practice 1.

steps.title: Start Claude Code in the practice folder

win.html:
1. Double-click the Practice folder on your desktop.
  2. Click the address bar at the top of the folder window, type powershell → Enter.
  3. Type claude in the window → Enter.

mac.html:
1. Open Terminal. (⌘ command+space → Terminal → return)
  2. Type cd and a space, drag the Practice folder onto the window, and press return.
  3. Type claude → return.

check.q: Do you see the box to type in (with a > sign)?

steps.title: If it doesn't start
steps.html:
• If you see 'claude' is not recognized, close and reopen the window, or restart the computer.
  • Not sure? See 'Open the window in the practice folder' in Terminal practice 1 again.

steps.title: Clear the conversation and start fresh — /clear
steps.html:
Type / (slash, the ? key at the bottom right of the keyboard) in the box and a list of commands appears. Things that start with / aren't requests to Claude; they're commands that control Claude Code itself.

Type the following and press Enter (return on a Mac).

steps.title: If /clear doesn't work
steps.html:
• The / must be the very first thing in the box. If there's other text before it, delete it and type again.
  • If a different character appears instead of /, check your keyboard is set to English.
  • When the list appears, press Enter with /clear selected.

steps.title: Check that it really forgot
steps.html: Let's ask whether Claude remembers what was said before.
steps.code: What were we just talking about?

check.q: Did Claude say something like 'there's no earlier conversation'?

faq.a: Claude may be guessing from the files it can see in the folder. That doesn't mean it remembers the conversation. You can run /clear once more and ask again.

steps.title: Done for the day! Close it and reopen
steps.html:
Pretend you've finished for today and close Claude Code.

  1. Type /exit in the box and press Enter (return on a Mac).
  2. Close the window.
  3. Pretend it's "the next day" and open the window again in the practice folder. (Same as step 2, but don't type claude yet.)

check.q: Did you open a new window in the practice folder? (without typing claude yet)

steps.title: Continue the conversation — claude -c
steps.html: This time, instead of claude, type the following and press Enter (return on a Mac). -c means "continue". Type it after claude with one space in between.
steps.alt: Starting with claude -c continues the last conversation

check.q: Do you see your last conversation ('What were we just talking about?') on screen?

steps.title: If it says there's no conversation to continue
steps.html:
• Conversations are saved separately for each folder. Make sure you opened the window in the practice folder.
  • Check there's one space between claude and -c.
  • If it still doesn't work, it's fine to start with plain claude and go on to the next step (/resume).

steps.title: Choose an older conversation — /resume
steps.html: Use this when you want to continue a conversation from a few days ago, not the last one. Type the following and press Enter (return on a Mac).
steps.alt: Choosing an older conversation from the /resume list

check.q: Did a list of older conversations appear? Choose one with ↑↓ and press Enter.

faq.q: There's only one conversation in the list.
faq.a: That's normal. It just means that's all you've had in the practice folder. If you did Practices 1 and 2 in the same folder, those conversations show up too.

faq.q: Can I choose right when I start?
faq.a: Yes. Start with claude -r instead of claude and the same list appears right away.

steps.title: If the list doesn't appear
steps.html:
• Check that you typed /resume exactly, at the very start of the box.
  • To close the list, press Esc.
  • It's okay if this doesn't work. Today's key points are /clear and claude -c.

steps.title: 🎉 Terminal practice 3 done! What you learned
steps.html:
Now you can split your work up, or come back days later, and carry on.

Which one, when?

Starting something different/clear — clears only the chat; files stay
Continuing yesterday's workStart with claude -c — in the same folder
Picking a conversation from days ago/resume (or start with claude -r)

Two things to remember

  1. Claude remembers earlier messages only within the same conversation.
  2. Conversations are saved separately for each folder. To continue, always start in the same folder.

Next step

Next you'll organize several files at once and learn to read a new permission screen: "May I run this command?"
